coverage.summary: Applies to any person (as defined in Bus. & Prof. Code § 16702, excluding the end consumer of a product or service) in any industry, including apartment rental companies. The statute sets no building, unit-count, construction-date or owner-type limits.

evidence.quoted_span: (5) “Person” has the same meaning as defined in Section 16702 and does not include the end consumer of a product or service.
Certain industries have been targets of recent federal algorithmic price fixing claims, including apartment rental companies,
Businesses in these industries should expect possible scrutiny under state law, but any business relying on a common pricing algorithm could be a target.

result.notes: I cleared other_conditions. The 'two or more persons' and 'competitor data' elements belong to the definition of a common pricing algorithm, which is the prohibited conduct. They do not describe a building, unit or owner, and the rule's requirement field already captures them. I reworded the summary to describe who is covered rather than the prohibited conduct. All other fields stay null because the documents set no building, unit, construction-date or owner-size conditions. Subd. (c) preserves other antitrust laws, but nothing in the documents addresses how the statute interacts with local ordinances, so the preemption and yield fields stay null.
